correctness.rationale: Over A=C⊕C with p=(1,0), q=(0,1), H=A and K=Ap, P(h)=ph has adjoint the inclusion. For every adjointable A-linear T:H→K, T(P*P)=T, yielding T P*P T*=TT* exactly: {P} is an operator-module Parseval frame. But Pq=0 and <q,q>=q>0 violate every positive lower g-frame bound. The nonzero operator module contains P. For any coefficient module with <e,e>=1, the rank-one map R_y(h)=<h,y>e is adjointable and satisfies R_y*e=y, giving a sufficient reachability repair.

value.rationale: The 2018/2021 paper presents the frame/g-frame equivalence as a main structural generalization. A nonzero Parseval operator-module frame over the smallest split unital C*-algebra disproves its converse, and the rank-one sufficient hypothesis isolates the lost reachability mechanism. This is a motivated correction of a substantive published theorem rather than a routine isolated normalization check.
